children: H.B. Fuller reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 results with net revenue of $938.2 million, up 5.2% year‑over‑year, and adjusted EBITDA of $186.7 million, a 9% increase versus prior year. The company posted net income attributable to H.B. Fuller of $79.2 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.52, up 21% year‑over‑year. Management noted pricing execution and restructuring savings drove margin expansion as the company advances its Quantum Leap program and expects the AMS acquisition to close before year‑end.
Net revenue: $938.2 million for the three months ended August 29, 2026, up 5.2% from $892.0 million a year earlier.
Gross profit: $311.7 million; gross margin 33.2% for Q3 2026 (adjusted gross profit $314.6 million; adjusted gross margin 33.5%).
Operating income (total segment operating income): $113.2 million for Q3 2026 (consolidated total operating income reported as $113,205 thousand).
Net income attributable to H.B. Fuller: $79.2 million for Q3 2026 (basic EPS $1.46; diluted EPS $1.44).
Adjusted EBITDA: $186.7 million for Q3 2026 (adjusted EBITDA margin 19.9%); adjusted diluted income per share $1.52 for the quarter.
Organic revenue growth: Organic revenue increased 4.4% year‑over‑year driven by pricing gains that more than offset lower volumes; pricing contributed 7.4% to net revenue growth in the quarter.

Segment performance: All three global business units—Hygiene, Health and Consumable Adhesives; Engineering Adhesives; and Building Adhesive Solutions—delivered organic revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA and margin improvement.
Operational improvements: Adjusted gross margin expanded by 120 basis points year‑over‑year, primarily from pricing execution and restructuring savings tied to the company’s Quantum Leap program.

Working capital and supply continuity: Net working capital rose to 18.5% of annualized net revenue due to strategic inventory investments to support Quantum Leap and ensure supply continuity amid regional disruptions.

Capital deployment and balance sheet: Net debt was $1,957.3 million at quarter end with net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA of 3.0x (trailing twelve months adjusted EBITDA $656.5 million); management noted the anticipated closing of the AMS acquisition before year‑end.
